sentences.en: Saturday afternoon, a friend treated me to a movie, and we bought two tickets.
The movie was pretty good when it started, but after half an hour, I found it really boring.
My friend said too: "This movie is so boring, so dull, I'm about to fall asleep."
I glanced at my watch — only forty minutes had passed. I thought to myself: there's still a whole hour left.
The movie wasn't even over yet, and we walked out of the cinema together.
The weather outside was nice, so we went for a walk in a nearby park.
We sat in the park for a long time, chatting about all kinds of other things.

quiz.q: How does the narrator feel about the movie after half an hour?
What do the narrator and friend do before the movie ends?
a: Walk out and go to a park

quiz.q: What do they end up doing in the park?
a: Sit and chat about other things

grammar.e: 没意思 describes something with no fun or appeal — the opposite of 有意思 (interesting). It works for movies, classes, or anything dull.
grammar.x: 这个电影太没意思了。— This movie is way too boring.

grammar.e: 才 before an amount makes it feel smaller or slower than expected — here it stresses how little time has passed.
grammar.x: 才过了四十分钟。— Only forty minutes had passed.

grammar.p: 还没 + verb，……就…… (before X even happened, ...)
grammar.e: 还没 says something hasn't happened yet, and pairing it with 就 shows another action already cutting in.
grammar.x: 电影还没结束，我们就走出了电影院。— The movie hadn't even ended, and we already walked out of the cinema.
